central_claim.note: Ad's harm to perceptions and counter-stereotype's mitigation; omits the representation improvement. 'Stigmatizing labels for Trump' keeps the case; not flagged.

evidence.note: E2: total N and three arms. E1 partial: no Prolific, pre-registration or dates. E3 partial: ad labeled 'CONVICTED CRIMINAL' (no mugshot) and counter-narrative about a formerly system-involved state representative (no news excerpt).

flags.text: Says the ad 'increases perceived self-interest motives of elected officials'. The paper finds the ad increased belief that officials are motivated by public service over self-interest (p.11, beta = 0.130), as the entry's own quote says.

key_findings.note: Only quote is not in the paper ('(positive)' inserted). The perceptions half would be F1; the motives half is wrong.

scope_and_limits.note: First quote (p.1, field experiments needed) is in the paper, so the entry is grounded; the second (full factorial) quote is not in the paper. Credited both parts under the one-faithful-quote rule.

theoretical_positioning.note: T1 with category salience and exemplars. 'Applies ... to predict' spillover from a prominent figure gives the 'applies' half of T4, not the extension/test.

interlocutor_claim.note: Accurate to p.2 (negative ads used less by poll leaders; Democrats respond more to positive ads); not a gold answer (same call as the calibration).
